source_text: Non solum iubet terrae proferre herbam foeni, sed et semen, ut semper fructum afferre possit; non solum lignum fructiferum, sed faciens fructum cuius semen in ipso est — omnium virtutum semina in corde nostro continere, ut ex ipsis actus secundum iustitiam geramus. Haec herba ad maturitatem veniat, altioribus in corde radicibus, ut fructum afferant et semina futurorum habeant.
pass_a_gloss: Not only he-orders to-earth to-bring-forth herb of-hay, but also seed, that always fruit to-bring it-may-be-able; not only tree fruit-bearing, but making fruit whose seed in itself is — of-all virtues seeds in heart our to-contain, that from them acts according-to justice we-may-carry. This herb to maturity let-come, with-deeper in heart roots, that fruit they-may-bring and seeds of-future-things they-may-have.
pass_b_english: He not only orders the earth to put forth grass, but also seed, so that it may always be able to bear fruit; not only a fruit tree, but one making fruit whose seed is in itself — that we keep the seeds of all the virtues in our heart, and from them carry out acts according to justice. Let this herb come to maturity with deeper roots in the heart, so that they bear fruit and hold seeds of what is to come.
